paper_title: Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs
core_problem: Large language models excel at mathematical reasoning and program synthesis but remain unable to effectively use tools via API calls. State-of-the-art LLMs such as GPT-4 struggle to generate accurate input arguments and tend to hallucinate incorrect API usage.
methodology_summary: Release Gorilla, a finetuned LLaMA-based model for writing API calls, and combine it with a document retriever to enable adaptation to test-time documentation changes and reduce hallucination. The retrieval-augmented setup allows flexible user updates or version changes.
datasets_eval: APIBench, a comprehensive dataset consisting of HuggingFace, TorchHub, and TensorHub APIs.
empirical_results: Gorilla surpasses GPT-4 on writing API calls. When combined with a document retriever, Gorilla demonstrates strong capability to adapt to test-time document changes, enabling flexible user updates or version changes, and substantially mitigates hallucination commonly encountered when prompting LLMs directly.
